territorial_scope.description: Amends a Malaysian statute; section 129 as amended governs transfers of personal data by data controllers to places outside Malaysia.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709) to rename “data user” as “data controller”, add data processor, data protection officer, breach notification, data portability and cross-border transfer rules, with commencement by ministerial notification in the Gazette.
summary.long: The Act amends the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709). It replaces “data user” with “data controller” throughout, adds “biometric data” and “personal data breach” to the definitions and makes biometric data sensitive personal data. Data processors must comply with the Security Principle, and the penalty for breaching section 5(1) rises to one million ringgit, imprisonment up to three years, or both. Data controllers must appoint data protection officers and notify the Commissioner of appointments (new section 12A). They must notify the Commissioner of personal data breaches as soon as practicable, and affected data subjects where significant harm is likely (new section 12B); breach of the Commissioner-notification duty is an offence with a fine up to 250,000 ringgit, imprisonment up to two years, or both. New section 43a gives data subjects a portability right, subject to technical feasibility and data-format compatibility. Section 129 is amended so that a data controller may transfer personal data abroad, deleting the Minister's power to specify destinations. Commencement is by ministerial notification in the Gazette, with different dates possible for different provisions. Existing Commissioner orders and codes and pending proceedings are saved.

relations.note: The Act amends the principal Act throughout, in ss. 2 to 14. Only the amending provisions are annotated here.

evidence.quote: The Personal Data Protection Act 2010 [Act 709], which is referred to as the “principal Act” in this Act, is amended

notes: Front matter gives Royal Assent 9 October 2024 and Gazette publication 17 October 2024; these are not operative provisions. Commencement: s. 1(2) provides that the Minister appoints the date by Gazette notification and may appoint different dates for different provisions; no commencement date is stated in the text. The principal Act is not reproduced, so only the amendments are coded. Internal points for readers: s. 2 replaces 'data user' with 'data controller' generally, but excludes the 'register' definition (s. 3(a) amends it separately) and s. 9; s. 5 then amends s. 9 with 'data controller and a data processor' wording. Section 7 changes a word in the national-language text only, and s. 5(b)(iii) applies language-specific edits to the English text only. Section 14(3) continues pending proceedings under the unamended principal Act.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in this amending Act changes legal treatment. The ringgit amounts and imprisonment terms (ss 5(2)(ii) and 6 new s 12b(3)) are penalty maxima and belong in enforcement. The data portability period is left to be prescribed (new s 43a(3)), a procedural time limit. The commencement date is to be appointed by the Minister (s 1(2)), which is not a numeric threshold.
